summary: Owned units s0178–s0199 contain no birth, death, or age figures. The only explicit Chinese date-bearing life events are Liu Tan as 丹陽尹 with Xu Xun lodging and Wang Xizhi present; Wang Xizhi at leisure writing to Xie Wan as 吏部郎, then again after Xie Wan became 豫州都督; and a counterfactual naming of Chao Fu, Xu You, Ji, and Qi plus a retrospective naming of Lu Jia, Ban Si, and Yang Wangsun. The 345–349 Danyang window is not in the chapter and conflicts with the dated 永和三年十二月 appointment in 建康實錄, while 資治通鑑 already sends Liu Tan to 沔中 in 永和元年, so AD 345 is not a safe start for this capital gathering. Wang’s leisure start in conventional AD 355 follows the chapter’s own 永和十一年 vow, but the AD 361 end is not in 年五十九卒 and should not be treated as an explicit year; 書斷’s 昇平五年卒 is a later witness among competing death-year reconstructions. Xie Wan’s Yuzhou appointment and the second letter belong to 升平二年 (AD 358) in 晉書·穆帝紀 and 資治通鑑, not the exact year AD 359 used here; the defeat is 升平三年. Lu Jia, Ban Si, and Yang Wangsun are reception-only names in Wang’s letter; the imported Han floruits are not this chapter’s events and must not feed active hints.

The closed AD 345–349 interval treats early Yonghe as a tenure. 建康實錄 places the appointment, and this same lodging anecdote, under 永和三年十二月 (conventional AD 347; the lunar twelfth month can spill into AD 348 and was not converter-checked day by day). 資治通鑑 already titles him 丹楊尹 in 永和元年 but in that same year sends him to 監沔中諸軍事、領義成太守, so AD 345 is not a safe start for a Jiankang Yin household scene. Death by 永和五年 (AD 349) is a later terminus from 褚裒 still alive when Sun Chuo spoke of 劉真長死, not an explicit end in this passage. Do not keep 345 as a second invented endpoint. Preserve the 347 appointment against the possibly proleptic 345 title as competing witnesses, and keep 349 only as an onOrBefore death bound.
